formulas.formula: Budget one paycheck at a time and always know which bills it has to cover.
1. Setup: the year, your first payday, your usual weekly take-home pay and what's in checking now. Then plan your weekly spending and savings.
2. Bills: every monthly bill with its amount and due day (1 to 31).
3. Paycheck Planner: each week shows the bills due before your next payday, your weekly plan, and what's left. Type your real pay in Actual Pay.
4. Watch Running Balance: if it goes red, a big bill (like rent) lands in a week your paycheck can't cover. Set money aside the week before.
5. Spending: log what you spend. Each purchase goes to the pay week it falls in.
6. Dashboard: this week's paycheck, spending by category and the next bills due.
A bill counts in the week from your payday up to the day before your next payday.
Some months have 5 paydays. Bills only come once a month, so that extra check is a great time to save.
Bills due on the 29th, 30th or 31st move to the last day of shorter months.
Pick any date in Today's date on Setup to see that week on the Dashboard. Blank = today.
Clear the white cells on Bills, Paycheck Planner (Actual Pay and Notes) and Spending, then update Setup.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: money left, or a 5th paycheck.
Red: short this week, or something to check.
Thank you for your purchase! One week at a time.

=IF($R$4=0,"Check the year and first payday on Setup.","Week "&$R$4&": payday "&TEXT(INDEX('Paycheck Planner'!$C$9:$C$61,$R$4),"dddd, mmmm d")&IF('Setup'!$R$7<'Setup'!$R$5," (your first payday is coming up)","")&".")
The basics. Everything else uses these.
Blank = first Friday. A payday from last year also works: it moves to the same weekday this year.
After tax. Change single weeks on the Paycheck Planner.
Optional: pick a date to preview that week. Blank = today.
Money in your account before the first payday.
="First payday: "&TEXT(R5,"dddd, mmmm d, yyyy")&". Bills cost about "&TEXT('Bills'!C47*12/52,"$#,##0")&" a week; your plan uses "&TEXT(C24,"$#,##0")&"."
Your monthly bills. Due day 1 to 31: days past the end of a month move to its last day.
One row per payday. Bills Due = bills due from this payday up to the day before the next one. Type your real pay in Actual Pay.
What you spend. Each purchase counts toward the pay week it falls in.
Each payday counts in the month it lands in. Months with 5 paydays bring in an extra check.
